body.normal: Once the Certificate of Incorporation is issued, the company opens a bank account, receives its share capital, issues share certificates and files a few early forms, such as INC-20A to declare commencement of business and ADT-1 for its first auditor.
body.simple: After the company exists, we open its bank account, bring in the money for shares and file a few starting forms.
body.detail: The first months after incorporation follow a set order. The board holds its first meeting and appoints the first auditor within 30 days. The company opens a bank account and the subscribers pay for their shares. Share certificates (SH-1) are issued within 60 days. INC-20A, the declaration of commencement of business, is filed within 180 days and confirms the share money was received. Where a foreign parent paid for the shares, FC-GPR is reported to the RBI within 30 days of the shares being issued.
body.why: Several of these have fixed legal deadlines counted from the incorporation date, and the bank account and share money you arrange drive most of them.
